subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in auto-reply for non-allowlisted group senders, and what default, cooldown, raw-ID, and admin-contact semantics should it use?
rationale: The change turns a silent Telegram authorization denial into visible group output and likely adds config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding reply with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID behavior.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and satisfy the visibility need through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and keep logs, docs, and manual Telegram ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding reply with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and adjacent docs/config/channel history make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this Telegram authorization UX decision.
